body.html: Who Benjaporn Bungalow is for — the shortest way to put it: Benjaporn Bungalow is for people who want to visit Ko Si Chang on a budget, don't need luxury, but do want a clean bed, an easy-to-walk location, and a host who looks after you well · it's not a beachfront boutique resort with a bay-view pool or a design that photographs well from every angle, and it's not a beachfront place where you open the door onto the sand — it's a small property of about 14 bungalows sitting in the town area of the island, near the pier, the market, and restaurants · its position is very clear: it's a "budget base" that lets you spend all day exploring the island and come back to sleep comfortably · the voices from real reviews on Booking.com, TripAdvisor, and Thai travel-review pages line up on who fits here — couples on a two-day, one-night trip who aren't chasing luxury, groups of friends who split the room cost down to a couple of hundred baht each, small families bringing elders to make merit and tour the island, and foreign backpackers looking for a clean, friendly-priced stay on the island · those expecting a beachfront resort, a pool, or big-hotel service may want to think twice, because Benjaporn is a simple place selling cleanliness, value, and friendliness more than luxury or a view · put another way, it does its own job well within the budget it sets, which is why its review scores stay consistently good.

Location and getting there — Benjaporn Bungalow is located at 72/1 Moo 3, Tha Thaewawong, Ko Si Chang, Chonburi, in the town area of the island, which is the strength most reviews talk about · Ko Si Chang is a small island off the coast of Si Racha district, and getting here has its charm precisely because you have to take the ferry across, which is part of the experience · from Bangkok, you drive or take a bus to Ko Loi pier in Si Racha, about an hour and a half to two hours, then board a passenger ferry that runs on schedule, with a fare of around 50 baht per trip and a crossing of about 45 minutes · what impresses many reviewers is that the property offers a free shuttle from the pier on the island, which genuinely solves the problem of finding a ride on the island, especially for groups arriving together with luggage · the bungalows sit in a town where you can walk to the pier, market, and restaurants within 5–7 minutes, and it's a short walk up to Phra Chudadhuj Palace, the summer palace from the reign of King Rama V · on the island it's popular to rent a skylab three-wheeler or a motorbike to tour around, making it easy to stop at viewpoints like Chong Khao Khat, the Chao Pho Khao Yai Shrine, and Tham Phang beach, and the property also lends bikes for free for anyone who wants to cycle around nearby · one small note is that the bungalows aren't beachfront, so it's not a place where you open the door onto the sand, and you should check the schedule for the last ferry back to the mainland carefully, especially on weekdays and long weekends when the ferry can get full enough that you have to wait for the next run — so leave yourself extra time.

"The ferry took 45 minutes, and once we reached the island the property's vehicle picked us up right away — so convenient. The room was clean and the bed was softer and comfier than the price suggests · after dropping our bags we could walk out to eat and rent a vehicle to tour the island right away, then come back to a comfy sleep. Truly worth the price."

Room types and decor — Benjaporn Bungalow has about 14 bungalows in total, a small scale that makes the atmosphere feel friendly, more like staying at a relative's place than a hotel · the rooms come in several types, from a twin or large bed for two up to two-bedroom bungalows and family rooms that sleep several people, which suit groups of friends or families wanting to split the cost · some units have a balcony or a sitting nook out front, and some upstairs units catch a sea view in the distance · the decor leans simple, in a bright, clean tone rather than a flashy design, with basic, practical furniture and amenities · the point real reviews praise most consistently is that the rooms are clean and the beds are wider and comfier than the price suggests — many say they slept very well, which is the most important thing for a stay at this price · the rooms have the basic conveniences covered, including air conditioning, a TV, and a sitting area · to be straight with you, the thing to know is that the design and furniture are simple for the price, not a boutique-style room that photographs well from every angle, and some reviews mention bathroom drainage in some units, where water pools on the floor after a shower, a limitation you'll find at simple island stays · for anyone who cares about a sea view or a balcony, you should ask and specify the room type when booking, because each unit gets a different view and amount of space · overall, judged on "cleanliness and comfort for the price," Benjaporn's rooms do well within the island's budget category.

Amenities and on-island services — to be straight from the start, Benjaporn Bungalow has no pool and isn't a resort with a gym or spa — it's a simple bungalow focused mainly on the bed and the location, so anyone hunting for a sea-view pool should set expectations correctly from the outset · but what the property does have, and reviews praise often, are the services that make exploring the island easy: a free shuttle from the pier, free parking (for those who leave their car on the Si Racha side and cross over), free Wi-Fi, and what many love — free loaner bikes for cycling around the nearby town · the property also helps arrange skylab or motorbike rentals and recommends spots to visit on the island, small details that put first-time travelers at ease · on top of that, being in the town means everything you need — convenience stores, restaurants, and the market — is within walking distance, so you don't need to rely much on the property's own amenities · a note found in reviews is that the Wi-Fi signal is weak in some rooms, a limitation common on small islands, so anyone who needs the internet for work may want to bring a backup SIM · overall, Benjaporn's amenities suit using the property as a base to head out and explore rather than as a destination to lounge in all day, which matches how most people do Ko Si Chang anyway.

Food and breakfast — Benjaporn Bungalow offers breakfast for guests, with the menu reviews mention being a simple set like eggs, sausage, ham, and coffee, made fresh in the morning · many reviews say the breakfast is tasty and gets the day off to a good start in a simple way, but some are honest that it's a small set, not as varied as a big-hotel buffet, which is reasonable for the size and price of the property · what keeps food from being a problem at all is the town location, within easy walking distance of restaurants and the market · Ko Si Chang is known for fresh, reasonably priced seafood, with made-to-order eateries, coffee shops, and snack stalls spread through the town, so many people eat out as their main plan · in the evening it's popular to take a skylab to eat seafood by the sea or stop at one of the island's well-known spots, which is the charm of staying in town that beachfront places far from town may not pull off as easily · the thing to know is that many restaurants on the island close earlier than in the city, so if you plan a late dinner you should check closing times ahead, or keep some snacks in your room · for anyone visiting Ko Si Chang with seafood and good local eats in mind already, Benjaporn's location has a clear edge here.

Service — service is where Benjaporn Bungalow draws the heaviest praise in real reviews · a great many use words like the staff and host are friendly, smiling, and attentive, whether it's coordinating the pier shuttle, recommending places to visit on the island, or helping with vehicle rentals · because it's a small property of about 14 units, guests feel looked after up close and personally, a charm small town properties pull off better than big hotels · the free shuttle from the pier is the detail many say impressed them most, because it cuts out the hassle of finding a ride on the island, which can be hard at certain times · many foreign travelers in TripAdvisor reviews also praise the place as safe, friendly, and genuinely welcoming · to be straight with you, since it's a small place run family-style, some service standards may be less formal than a chain hotel's, and replies to online bookings can sometimes be slower than on the big OTAs — but overall, the friendliness and care are the clearest strengths here.

Voices from real reviews (praise and gripes) — pulling from Booking.com, TripAdvisor, and Thai travel-review pages, the picture is fairly consistent and leans positive · on the praise side: clean rooms and wide, comfy beds beyond the price, a town location a few minutes' walk from the pier, market, and restaurants, a very convenient free pier shuttle, free loaner bikes, fresh-made breakfast like eggs, sausage, ham, and coffee, friendly and attentive staff and host, a quiet, relaxing atmosphere, and the value for money many single out as a highlight · on the gripe side: what comes up is that the design and furniture are simple and basic for the price, not a boutique-style stay, bathroom drainage in some units pools on the floor after a shower, the Wi-Fi signal is weak in some rooms, the property isn't beachfront and has no pool, and the breakfast is a small set, not as varied as a big hotel's · most of these gripes are things you can manage by setting expectations right and preparing a little, rather than big problems that keep people from returning, which is reflected in an overall score that stays good and a #2 ranking among small properties on the island on TripAdvisor.

"The place was clean, the staff lovely and very friendly, with a vehicle to pick us up from the pier, and it was easy to walk out to eat and explore · the only small gripes were that the bathroom drained a bit slowly and the in-room internet was weak, but for this price on the island it's really worth it. I'll be back."

Price comparison and value — Benjaporn Bungalow's starting price is around ฿1,100/night in the normal range, climbing on weekends or long holidays to around ฿1,500–2,000+ per night depending on room type and timing · for rooms that sleep several people, like the family bungalow, splitting the cost among friends comes out to just a couple of hundred baht each, which is why many reviews single out value as a highlight · compared with other stays on Ko Si Chang, Benjaporn falls into the group of budget town stays with easy-to-reach prices, considerably cheaper than a beachfront boutique resort like Somewhere Koh Sichang, which starts at around ฿1,900 and up · what Benjaporn gives you is cleanliness, a comfy bed, an easy-to-walk location, and a free shuttle, at a lighter price · what you trade away is no pool, no beachfront, and a simple design · so if the goal of the trip is to tour the island, make merit, eat seafood, and save on accommodation to spend the budget on exploring, Benjaporn is a worthwhile, well-balanced choice · but if you want a sea-view resort vibe with a pool to soak in all day, you may need to up the budget toward the boutique group instead.

What to know before booking — a few things help make the stay smoother · one, specify the room type and number of people clearly when booking, because each bungalow differs in size and view, and if you want an upstairs room that catches a bit of sea you should ask ahead · two, the property has no pool and isn't beachfront, so set expectations correctly that this is a town bungalow to use as a base for exploring · three, bring a backup SIM or internet, because some reviews say the in-room Wi-Fi is weak · four, make the most of the free pier shuttle, and tell the property ahead of time when you'll reach the pier · five, check the ferry schedule from Ko Loi pier in Si Racha carefully, especially the last run and long-weekend periods when the ferry can be full · six, for booking, besides Agoda and Booking.com, the property also takes direct bookings via the Facebook page "Benjaporn Bungalow Ko Si Chang" and by phone at 097-127-2586, which may sometimes get you a better price or more flexible terms · seven, plan some dinners ahead because restaurants on the island close earlier than in the city.

The bottom line — from all the real reviews, Benjaporn Bungalow is best suited to people who want to visit Ko Si Chang on a budget but want a clean bed, an easy-to-walk location, and a host who looks after them well · clean rooms, wide comfy beds, a town location within walking distance of the pier and restaurants, a free pier shuttle, and free loaner bikes make it a top choice on Ko Si Chang in the easy-to-reach price group, and the reason its review scores stay consistently good enough to rank #2 among small properties on the island on TripAdvisor · if you're after a beachfront resort, a bay-view pool, or a boutique design that photographs well from every angle, this may not be the answer, and you should consider the island's boutique group instead · but for an island trip where you want to use the property as a base to make merit, hit the viewpoints, and eat seafood in town while paying little for the room — Benjaporn Bungalow fits that need well, and it's why so many guests say they'll be back.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Benjaporn Bungalow Ko Si Chang

faq.q: Where is Benjaporn Bungalow · how do you get there?
faq.a: The property is at 72/1 Moo 3, Tha Thaewawong, Ko Si Chang, Chonburi, in the town area of the island · get there by driving or taking a bus to Ko Loi pier in Si Racha (about 1.5–2 hours from Bangkok), then take the ferry across for a fare of around 50 baht, a 45-minute crossing · once on the island, the property has a free shuttle from the pier, and the bungalows are a 5–7 minute walk to the pier, market, and restaurants.

faq.q: What's Benjaporn Bungalow's starting price · what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at around ฿1,100/night for a large bed for two in the normal range · there are rooms with a balcony and family / two-bedroom bungalows that sleep several, with weekend prices climbing to around ฿1,500–2,000+ · there are about 14 units, so book ahead during long holidays.

Great for couples, groups of friends, and small families who want to visit Ko Si Chang on a budget while wanting a clean bed and an easy-to-walk location · best for using the property as a base to head out to make merit, hit the viewpoints, and eat seafood in town · if you're hunting for a beachfront resort with a pool, the island's boutique group may suit you better.

faq.q: Does Benjaporn Bungalow have a pool and breakfast?
faq.a: No pool, and the property isn't beachfront — it's a simple town bungalow · there is fresh-made breakfast like eggs, sausage, ham, and coffee, which reviews say is tasty in a simple way but is a small set, not as varied as a big-hotel buffet · the town location makes it easy to walk out to restaurants and the market.

faq.q: Are there any things to know about Benjaporn Bungalow before booking?
faq.a: From real reviews, the things to know are that the property isn't beachfront and has no pool, best used as a base for exploring · the design and furniture are simple for the price · bathroom drainage in some units pools on the floor after a shower · the Wi-Fi signal is weak in some rooms, so bring a backup SIM · and you have to take the ferry across, so check the last-ferry schedule carefully.

faq.q: How can you book Benjaporn Bungalow?
faq.a: You can book via Agoda and Booking.com · the property also takes direct bookings via the Facebook page "Benjaporn Bungalow Ko Si Chang" and by phone at 097-127-2586, which may sometimes get you a better price or more flexible terms · it scores 8.8 on Booking.com and 4.5/5 on TripAdvisor, ranked #2 among small properties on the island.
